education.degree: BSc in Applied Mathematics; Minor in Computing

research.title: Research Assistant - Numerical Methods
description: Implemented finite-difference solvers for two-dimensional heat transport and checked convergence on analytic solutions.
Compared conjugate-gradient and multigrid solvers over four grid resolutions with fixed stopping criteria.
Measured a 2.1x runtime reduction for multigrid on the largest grid; reported setup cost and memory tradeoffs.
Used manufactured solutions to validate boundary handling and estimate empirical convergence rates.
Profiled sparse matrix assembly separately from iterative solution to identify where runtime improvements originated.
Analyzed stopping tolerances, conditioning and residual error rather than treating speed as the only objective.
Wrote a 24-page internal report describing discretization assumptions, numerical stability and reproducibility.

research.title: Undergraduate Thesis - Optimization under Noise
description: Compared stochastic gradient and variance-reduction methods on synthetic convex objectives.
Reported sensitivity to step size and noise over 30 independent runs; produced a departmental thesis.
Derived baseline convergence expectations for smooth objectives and compared them with empirical trajectories.
Performed controlled experiments on batch size and noise variance, recording function evaluations as well as iterations.
Separated failed runs from successful runs and included sensitivity plots in the thesis appendix.
Led weekly Python problem sessions and reviewed solver correctness for 40 students.
Prepared exercises on floating-point error, iterative solvers and numerical differentiation.
Used reference solutions and unit tests to help students diagnose indexing and boundary-condition errors.
Maintained an anonymized issue log and revised examples after recurring misconceptions.

projects.name: Sparse Linear Algebra Benchmark Suite
description: Built benchmark scripts for runtime, residual error and memory use across sparse matrix families.
Published reproducible instructions and checks against reference solutions in a demonstration repository.
Included warm-up runs, repeated timing and explicit matrix sizes to reduce misleading benchmark comparisons.
Recorded solver failures and nonconvergence alongside successful timings.
Added a command-line interface and documented build flags, thread counts and reference tolerances.

projects.name: Optimization Learning Notebook Series
description: Created six teaching notebooks covering gradient methods, conditioning and constrained optimization.
Used synthetic counterexamples to demonstrate unstable step sizes and misleading stopping criteria.
Added reproducible figures and exercises comparing analytic and numerical gradients.
Collected feedback from 12 classmates and revised explanations of convergence diagnostics.

projects.name: PDE Solver Verification Lab
description: Implemented explicit and implicit time-stepping methods for one-dimensional diffusion.
Compared stability and error under controlled changes in grid spacing and timestep.
Verified boundary conditions using manufactured solutions and conservation checks.
Created plots distinguishing discretization error from floating-point effects.
Prepared reproducible notebooks explaining assumptions to classmates without a numerical-analysis background.

projects.name: Algorithmic Thinking Study Group
description: Organized an eight-week peer study group connecting mathematical proofs with executable algorithms.
Implemented graph traversal, dynamic programming and sparse matrix examples with reference tests.
Reviewed complexity arguments and documented differences between worst-case bounds and observed runtimes.
Maintained a shared repository with reproducible exercises and contributor notes.
Collected anonymous feedback and revised exercises that confused mathematical notation with implementation details.
